correctness.rationale: For all real μ,β>0 on the reflection-symmetric cubic subfamily, the crossing orbit equations for r,s∈(0,1/2) factor as μ(r−s)(1/4−r²−rs−s²)=0. Symmetric roots of Bμ(u)=(4+μ/2)u−2μu³ have exact counts at β=2 and β_f=(μ+8)^(3/2)/(6√(3μ)); nonsymmetric roots reduce to monotone Cμ(t)=2t[1+μ(t²−1/4)] on 1/2<t<1/√3, giving exactly two distinct oriented-crossing orbits only for 1<β<(μ+12)/(6√3). The β=1,β_sb,β_f and u=1/2 boundary exclusions follow from the strict domains. The exact multiplier (Λ(t)−1)=μ(3t²−1)(12μt²−μ+4)/4<0 and Λ→1 imply both asymmetric cycles attract on a nonempty left-neighborhood of β_sb; the symmetric orbit changes stability there. This is a crossing count, not a global two-cycle census.
